name: Scatter Chart
description: Hand-rolled SVG scatter plot with x/y axes, multi-series dots, and optional size encoding.
usage:
<ScatterChart
  aria-label="Latency by payload size"
  series={[{ name: "Baseline", data: [{ x: 12, y: 40 }, { x: 24, y: 55 }] }]}
  xAxisLabel="Payload (KB)"
  yAxisLabel="Latency (ms)"
/>

anatomy.description: X and Y lines with min/max tick labels and optional axis captions.
Palette-colored dot per data point with a tooltip of its x, y or a custom label.
Optional mapping of a third value to dot radius via sizeEncoding.

dos: Add xAxisLabel and yAxisLabel with units; bare min/max ticks lack context.
Provide point labels when individual points represent named entities.
Keep it to two or three series so the color groups stay readable.
donts: Don't use it for ordered time trends; LineChart connects the dots better.
Don't enable sizeEncoding without explaining nearby what the radius means.
Don't plot thousands of points; it is one SVG node per dot.

examples.title: Multi-series comparison
examples.description: Two series plotted against shared axes with palette-colored dots and per-point tooltips.

examples.title: Size-encoded bubbles
examples.description: A third numeric dimension mapped to dot radius via the sizeEncoding prop.

guidance.useWhen: You need to show correlation or distribution between two numeric variables, optionally weighted by a third.
guidance.avoidWhen: Values are categorical or time-ordered trends; use Sparkline or DataTable instead.
guidance.behavior: Purely presentational: axes scale to the data domain, each dot carries a native title tooltip, and an sr-only summary lists the series.
guidance.responsive: Renders at the given width and height; wrap it in a horizontally scrollable container at narrow widths.

notes: The chart is a single role="img" with an aria-label; a visually hidden summary lists series names and point counts.
Color distinguishes series, but every dot also has a text tooltip that names its series.
